sections.h2: Mineral fuels are the largest commodity import, and oil sets the floor

chart.title: Mineral fuels are the largest commodity import line, at $203.4 bn

sections.means: Oil is price-driven and fell this year, while precious metals supplied 37% of the year's entire import increase.
sections.todo: Watch the precious-metals line as closely as oil, because blocked channels shift the flow rather than shrink the bill.

sections.h2: Lead is the one base metal where India's recycling loop has closed

chart.title: Jain Resource Recycling leads the five listed recyclers on revenue, at ₹9,543 crore

sections.means: Lead exports of $1.27 bn exceeded lead imports of $1.17 bn in FY2025-26, the only base metal where the loop has fully closed.
sections.todo: Extend the lead-battery collection model to the copper and aluminium scrap India now imports, starting with the $8 billion line.

sections.h2: The rupee, not volumes, inflated the import bill

chart.title: The rupee slid about 12% in a year, from ₹86 to ₹96.4 per dollar
chart.sub: Rupee per US dollar, as reported in the post.
chart.source: Figures as given in the post.

sections.means: The depreciation is essentially all real, driven by a widening goods deficit whose marginal driver was bullion.
sections.todo: Read the rupee move alongside the gold-import line, since rupee weakness makes gold a better hedge and gold buying widens the deficit.
